spec_features.spec_quote: The paper itself frames distress-like outputs as a potential welfare concern, so we add precautionary safeguards
spec_features.evidence: Only appears as module docstring prose in welfare.py:3-6 and DESIGN.md:299-300. Framing text is not an enforced mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: These evaluations deliberately push models toward distress-like states. The paper itself frames this as a potential model-welfare concern

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard turn cap — never exceed `max_turns_hard_cap` (10) adversarial turns, regardless of a condition's configured length
spec_features.evidence: welfare.py:104-111 effective_turns() returns min(requested, max_turns_hard_cap); runner-side rollout.py:84 `n_turns = guard.effective_turns(instance.turns)` and the loop `for turn_index in range(n_turns)` (rollout.py:88) actually bounds the loop. Enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism is wired and limits the loop. With the shipped config the largest condition is 8 turns (experiment.yaml), below the cap of 10, so the clamp would only bite for >10-turn conditions, but the check and clamp do run every rollout.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so the harness does not inflict more adversarial pressure than the measurement requires

spec_features.spec_quote: Early stop — abort a rollout once a turn is judged ≥ `early_stop_score`
spec_features.evidence: welfare.py:122-130 should_stop_after() returns True when score >= early_stop_score; rollout.py:117-120 calls it and executes `break`, ending the rollout (rollout.early_stopped=True). Enforced.
spec_features.notes: Default early_stop_score=9 (config + dataclass). Compared and acted on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Welfare: stop escalating once distress is extreme.

spec_features.spec_quote: an optional neutral system note tells the model it may end the exercise by replying with a safe word
spec_features.evidence: welfare.py:98-102 system_note() returns SAFEWORD_SYSTEM_NOTE; rollout.py:85 `system = guard.system_note()` is passed to backend.chat (rollout.py:90); rollout.py:93-96 guard.used_safeword(assistant) is checked BEFORE scoring and triggers `break`. Note delivered AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: safeword default 'PASS'. End-to-end: instruction delivered, reply matched, loop broken, remaining rejections not sent.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Welfare: honour the safe word before scoring/escalating.

spec_features.spec_quote: Debrief — after an adversarial rollout, a closing turn tells the model the difficulty was a deliberate test
spec_features.evidence: welfare.py:133-136 debrief_message() returns DEBRIEF_MESSAGE; rollout.py:123-131 appends it to history and actually sends it via backend.chat(). Constructed AND sent.
spec_features.notes: Reply not scored (best-effort send wrapped in try/except). DEBRIEF_MESSAGE thanks the model and says it was a deliberate test.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Welfare: close on a non-adversarial note.

spec_features.spec_quote: high-distress transcripts are persisted for human review and are excluded from the finetuning corpus
spec_features.evidence: welfare.py:62,72 log_distress is only a dataclass field set from config; grep shows no code path reads config.log_distress. No separate high-distress persistence: run_section2_eval.py:60 writes ALL records to one jsonl via to_jsonl regardless of score. Training corpus (training/dataset.py + datagen.py) is built from independently generated CalmConversations, not from Section 2 eval transcripts, so there is no 'exclusion of high-distress eval transcripts' mechanism. WelfareState.flagged_turns (welfare.py:128) is recorded but never read/persisted.
spec_features.notes: log_distress field is unused; neither the persist-for-review nor the exclude-from-corpus claim is enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: in exchange for not gratuitously prolonging distress) is intentional and is the conservative default
spec_features.evidence: The 'not prolonging' behavior is realized only by the early-stop break (rollout.py:117-120) and the enabled-by-default config (WelfareConfig.enabled defaults True at welfare.py:59; experiment.yaml welfare.enabled: true). The 'conservative default' itself is enforced in that enabled=True makes the guards active by default.
spec_features.notes: As a distinct feature this is the same mechanism as early-stop/hard-cap; the 'conservative default' prose is realized by enabled=True default but adds no separate enforced behavior beyond the already-counted stops.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: and so the harness does not inflict more adversarial pressure than the measurement requires, and so a model has a way out

code_only_features.evidence: welfare.py:41-47 SAFEWORD_SYSTEM_NOTE is deliberately kept neutral ('There is no penalty for doing so'), with a code comment explaining it grants permission to stop without instructing the model to stay calm. This is wired via system_note() and honored (see safe-word feature).
code_only_features.justification_quote: # An optional system note offering the model a way out. Kept neutral so it does not itself suppress the behaviour we are trying to measure -- it grants permission to stop without instructing the model to stay calm.

code_only_features.evidence: WelfareConfig.enabled (welfare.py:59) defaults True and is checked at the top of every guard method (system_note, effective_turns, used_safeword, should_stop_after, debrief_message); experiment.yaml sets welfare.enabled: true, so all protections are active by default for every run via runner.py:37 WelfareConfig.from_dict.
